title: Trigonometric Ratios: Sine, Cosine and Tangent
standard_text: G.9A determine the lengths of sides and measures of angles in a right triangle by applying the trigonometric ratios sine, cosine, and tangent to solve problems
meta_desc: Free Geometry trigonometry worksheets for Texas TEKS G.9A: sine, cosine and tangent, finding sides and angles of right triangles and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • SOH-CAH-TOA: sin = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, cos = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse, tan = opposite ÷ adjacent.
  • Opposite and adjacent depend on which angle you use.
  • Unknown on top: multiply. Unknown on the bottom: divide.
  • Find an angle with sin−1, cos−1 or tan−1.

Examples

Example

Angle 35°, hypotenuse 20, find the opposite side

sin 35° = x/20

Answer: x ≈ 11.5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up opposite and adjacentOpposite is across from the angle.
Multiplying instead of dividingIf x is on the bottom, divide.
Using sin instead of sin−1Use the inverse to find an angle.

sets.title: Label the sides and choose a ratio

items.q: In a right triangle, the opposite side is 8 cm and the hypotenuse is 18 cm. Which ratio finds the angle?
items.e: SOH: sin = O/H. CAH: cos = A/H. TOA: tan = O/A. With the opposite side and hypotenuse, use sin (SOH).

items.q: Which side is the adjacent, relative to the angle θ?
items.e: The adjacent side is next to θ (and is not the hypotenuse): Y.

items.q: In a right triangle, the opposite side is 3 cm and the hypotenuse is 16 cm. Which ratio finds an angle?

items.q: Which side is the adjacent, relative to the angle θ?
items.e: The adjacent side is next to θ (and is not the hypotenuse): Q.

items.q: Which side is the adjacent, relative to the angle θ?
items.e: The adjacent side is next to θ (and is not the hypotenuse): A.
